subject: Student Inclusion and Disability Awareness Curriculum
overview: The subcommittee established "meaningful inclusion and building friendships" as its primary focus for the year. Members reviewed updates on the district's disability awareness curriculum pilot and discussed expanding inclusive social and service opportunities for middle school students.

items.title: Subcommittee Schedule and Format
items.summary: The subcommittee established a staggered meeting schedule, alternating monthly between special education and behavioral health topics to allow for work on specific concerns between sessions.

items.title: Defining the Problem of Practice
items.summary: Members identified meaningful inclusion and building student friendships through school and recreational programming as the primary focus for the year.

items.title: Collaborative Recreational Programming
items.summary: The group discussed expanding unified sports and collaborating with Medford Recreation to offer inclusive summer programming and adaptive activities.

items.title: Disability Awareness Curriculum and Reverse Inclusion Update
items.summary: Director of Pupil Services Joan Bowen updated the committee on the disability awareness curriculum pilot currently active across three grade levels and the continuation of the Common Ground reverse inclusion program at the high school.

items.title: Middle School Inclusive Service Project
items.summary: Member Mea Quinn Mustone proposed an inclusive middle school service project in partnership with the Bread of Life, and the committee clarified that specialized transportation must be provided to ensure student access to after-school activities.

items.title: Future Planning and Research Assignments
items.summary: The subcommittee assigned research tasks regarding the Best Buddies program, recreational partnerships, and curriculum data collection for report-back at the January meeting.
